answer: An island monitoring market handles echo soundings and ember alerts. It can assign subsidized jobs by drawing from locked credit units rather than agent names. Register deposits before an unpredictable beacon, freeze them until the allocation period ends, and give each unit equal weight. Ten keys splitting one deposit get no more total chance than one key. Capturing more slots requires locking more capital and paying its financing cost. This assumes deposits cannot back simultaneous draws elsewhere and no account receives a free minimum allocation.
